**Temporal focus:**

T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES] — ongoing risk through coming months
T3. Long-term development [YES] — multi-decade permafrost/glacier degradation trend tied to climate change

**Synopsis:**
The summer of 2026 has set a new record of 450 rockfalls in the Mont Blanc massif, surpassing the previous 2022 record of 300. CNRS geomorphologist Ludovic Ravanel attributes this to extreme heat (30–35°C+), permafrost thaw, and glacier retreat — the latter removing stabilising pressure on rock faces. 80–85% of identified rock-face scarring has occurred in the past 2–3 decades. Three fatalities (two Czech tourists + one other) were recorded. No access restrictions planned, but vigilance urged.
